subject: Economics
description: Covers Primary/Tertiary sectors and Disguised unemployment.

questions.stem: In the context of the Indian economy, which sector is referred to as the 'Primary Sector'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Primary Sector involves the direct extraction or harvesting of natural resources from the earth. This includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining. It forms the base for all other products.
DECOY BUSTING: Manufacturing is the Secondary Sector. Services (banking, transport) form the Tertiary Sector. Research & Development is often classed as the Quaternary Sector.
EXAM INSIGHT: Even though the Primary Sector contributes the LEAST to India's GDP (around 18-20%), it famously employs the LARGEST portion of the Indian workforce (around 45%), highlighting a massive productivity/underemployment issue in agriculture.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities falls under the 'Tertiary Sector' of the economy?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Tertiary Sector is the service sector. It doesn't produce physical goods; instead, it provides services that support the primary and secondary sectors and the general population. Banking, insurance, transport, trade, healthcare, and education all fall under this sector.
DECOY BUSTING: Textile manufacturing is Secondary (processing raw materials). Mining and dairy farming are Primary (extracting from nature).
EXAM INSIGHT: The Tertiary sector is the undisputed backbone of the modern Indian economy, contributing over 50% to the total GDP, largely driven by the IT/BPO boom since the 1990s.

questions.stem: The phenomenon of 'Disguised Unemployment' is most commonly observed in which sector of the Indian economy?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed in a job than are actually required to do it. If some workers are removed, total production does not decrease because their marginal productivity is zero. In India, this is rampant in agriculture, where an entire family of 6 might work on a small farm that only really needs 2 people to tend it.
DECOY BUSTING: IT, Manufacturing, and Banking usually suffer from 'Cyclical' unemployment (due to recessions) or 'Structural' unemployment (due to changing skills), but rarely disguised unemployment as private companies won't pay extra unneeded workers.
EXAM INSIGHT: Another common type of rural unemployment is 'Seasonal Unemployment', where farmers have no work during the off-season (months when no crops are sown or harvested).
